blocks.text: A1-06 · Questions
Lesson overview

Who? What? Where? When? How many? With this unit learn to ask questions and answer, and read and fill out a form with personal data. Arab questions have a rule that simplifies everything: they are always at the beginning of the sentence, and the rest does not change. For questions yes/no just put ⁧هَلْ⁩ in the face of a statement.

rows: 6–7 hours · one week (week 21 of the calendar)

blocks.text: Materials This unit, Anki deck A1 (tag A1-06), script for speech synthesis, session with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. ask questions yes/no with ⁧هَلْ⁩ and answer with ⁧نَعَمْ⁩ / ⁧لَا⁩ ;
2. use ⁧مَا، مَاذَا، مَنْ، أَيْنَ، كَيْفَ، مَتَى، كَمْ، لِمَاذَا⁩ ;
3. ask and give personal data: first name, surname, age, address, work, telephone;
4. use ⁧كَمْ⁩ by the name to the singular: ⁧كَمْ طَالِبًا؟⁩ ;
5. read and fill out a simple form;
6. understand a slow interview and ask eight questions to the tutor.
Plan of the week.

rows: Dialogue 1 · sections 1–2: ⁧هَلْ⁩ and questions · lexicon (first half)
Section 5: personal data · reading the form · exercises 4–5

What to notice. Each question begins with the question and then follows a normal nominal phrase: ⁧أَيْنَ⁩ + ⁧بَيْتُكَ⁩ , ⁧مَتَى⁩ + . ⁧الدَّرْسُ القَادِمُ⁩ The answer takes up the sentence without the question. ⁧عُمْر⁩ means age (Lett. "Life": ... how old are you?... is it what your age is?
2. Questions yes/no: ⁧هَلْ⁩
To turn a statement into a question you put ⁧هَلْ⁩ It's the beginning. Nothing else changes: neither order nor words.
. ⁧فِي الشَّارِعِ صَيْدَلِيَّةٌ⁩ ⁧هَلْ فِي الشَّارِعِ صَيْدَلِيَّةٌ؟⁩ . ⁧نَعَمْ⁩

Before the Article ⁧هَلْ⁩ Takes the support: ⁧هَلِ المَكْتَبُ قَرِيبٌ؟⁩ hali l-maktabu qarīb? Without ⁧هَلْ⁩ . In the talk you ask questions even with the ascending intonation (you saw it in A1-02 and A1-05); in writing the question yes/no opens with ⁧هَلْ⁩ . To be recognized: . ⁧أَ⁩ In literary and journalistic texts the question yes/no can begin with the hamza ⁧أَ⁩ attached to the word: ⁧أَأَنْتَ مُتَرْجِمٌ؟⁩ Are you an interpreter? It is frequent especially in the face of a negation (A1-16).
3. Questions

rows: What? (in front of names and pronouns)
Where are you from? (to a woman)

blocks.text: ⁧مَا⁩ or ⁧مَاذَا⁩ ? In standard Arabic the choice depends on what follows: ⁧مَا⁩ before a name or pronoun ( ⁧مَا اسْمُكَ؟، مَا هٰذَا؟⁩ ), ⁧مَاذَا⁩ before a verb ( ⁧مَاذَا تَدْرُسُ؟⁩ What are you studying? Verbs arrive in A1-13: for now ⁧مَاذَا تَدْرُسُ؟⁩ and ⁧مَاذَا تَعْمَلُ؟⁩ "What work do you do?" are blocks to learn whole. ⁧أَيّ⁩ is followed by an indeterminate name to the genitive: ⁧أَيُّ مَكْتَبٍ؟⁩ - which office? ⁧أَيُّ سَيَّارَةٍ؟⁩ - Which car? Recognize him; you will actively use it in A2. How to respond to ⁧لِمَاذَا⁩ . The answer begins with ⁧لِأَنَّ⁩ li-anna ... why: the complete construction you will see in A2. For now you can answer with a name: ⁧لِمَاذَا أَنْتَ هُنَا؟⁩ — ⁧لِلدَّرْسِ⁩ li-d-dars
4. : ⁧كَمْ⁩ How many?
After ⁧كَمْ⁩ the name goes to the singular, indeterminate, with the desinence -an (accusative):

rows: How many students are in the class?
How many cars are on the street?

blocks.text: ⁧كَمْ سَنَةً فِي مِيلَانُو؟⁩ kam sanatan fī Mīlānū? How old are you in Milan?

Because the singular. For Arabic, how many people are asked to count unity: the unit is appointed, to the singular. The accusation case (-an) you will study it in A1-19; here remembers the shape with the alif of tanwīn: ⁧طَالِبًا⁩ , ⁧سَيَّارَةً⁩ ( ⁧ة⁩ the alif is not written). Age. ⁧كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟⁩ / ⁧كَمْ عُمْرُكِ؟⁩ How old are you? (to a man/a woman). Answer ⁧عُمْرِي⁩ … ⁧سَنَةً⁩ : ⁧عُمْرِي عِشْرُونَ سَنَةً⁩ I'm 20 years old. ⁧عُمْرِي ثَلَاثُونَ سَنَةً⁩ I'm 30 years old. The numbers are in A1-11; there you will also find dozens and numbers composed to say any age.

8. Pronunciation

. ⁧هَلْ⁩ The initial h and the final are pronounced: hal, not al. In front of the article: hali l- . The lengths of questions. ⁧مَا⁩ , ⁧مَاذَا⁩ , ⁧مَتَى⁩ have the ā long; ⁧مَنْ⁩ and ⁧كَمْ⁩ I'll see you soon. but short in ⁧مَا⁩ change the rhythm of the question: keep it long. . ⁧مَتَى⁩ It's written with alif. maqṣūra (L0-09) but read matā . ⁧ع⁩ of ⁧عُمْر⁩ and ⁧عُنْوَان⁩ . Two words of modules starting with ʿayn: ʿumr , ʿunwān . Without ʿayn They become incomprehensible. The pitch. With ⁧هَلْ⁩ the question is already marked: the intonation remains quite flat. With open questions the emphasis falls on the question: AYna l-maḥaṭṭa?
9. New lexicon

Notes of use. ⁧عُنْوَان⁩ also means "title" (of a book, of an article). ⁧مَسَاءً⁩ is written without final alif because the word ends in hamza after an alif (L0-09). ⁧أَوَّل⁩ has an irregular female, ⁧أُولَى⁩ : ⁧الدَّرْسُ الأَوَّلُ⁩ , ⁧المَرَّةُ الأُولَى⁩ The first time is the first time. ⁧سُؤَال⁩ You've already met him in the titles of L0-10: here it enters the active vocabulary.

14. Oral production
1. Repeat. Repeat the B script questions with the right intonation, then answer them instead of Laylā.
2. Interview with the tutor. Ask the tutor the eight questions for the exercise 8 and take notes in Arabic. Then the tutor interview you.
3. To the door. Recite the dialog 2 with the tutor: you are the employee, the tutor a user who responds with data invented; fill out the form while you listen.
